artists.biography:
Mental As Anything are an Australian new wave/pop/rock band formed at an art school in Sydney in 1976. Its most popular line-up (which lasted from 1977-1999) was Martin Plaza (birth name Martin Murphy) on vocals and guitar; Reg Mombassa (birth name Chris O'Doherty) on lead guitar and vocals; his brother Peter "Yoga Dog" O'Doherty on bass guitar and vocals; Wayne "Bird" Delisle (birth name David Twohill) on drums; and Andrew "Greedy" Smith on vocals, keyboards and harmonica.

Their top ten Australian singles are "If You Leave Me, Can I Come Too?" and "Too Many Times" (both from 1981), "Live It Up" (1985) and "Rock and Roll Music" (1988). Internationally, "Too Many Times" made the Canadian top 40 in 1982, and "Live It Up" peaked at No. 3 in UK, No. 4 in Norway, and No. 6 in Germany, after it featured in the 1986 Australian film "Crocodile" Dundee.

All of the early members are visual artists and have had combined studio displays, some have had solo studio displays with Mombassa's artwork also used as designs by the Mambo clothing company. The majority of the group's record covers, posters and video clips have been designed and created by themselves or their art school contemporaries. On 27 August 2009, Mental As Anything was inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) Hall of Fame alongside Kev Carmody, The Dingoes, Little Pattie and John Paul Young.

perplexity.description:
Fundamental" is the fifth studio album by Australian rock/pop band Mental As Anything, originally released in March 1985 on Regular Records. Produced by Richard Gottehrer, the album showcases a blend of pop and new wave styles, reflecting the band's evolving sound during the mid-1980s. Recorded at Rhinoceros Studios in Sydney, "Fundamental" features contributions from all four band songwriters, resulting in a diverse collection of tracks that balance catchy melodies with rock and new wave influences.

In the context of Mental As Anything's discography, "Fundamental" marked a commercial peak, reaching No. 3 on the Australian Kent Music Report albums chart and earning double platinum certification for sales exceeding 140,000 units in Australia. The album's success solidified the band's presence in the Australian rock scene of the 1980s and demonstrated their ability to produce accessible yet artistically varied music. While initially released on Regular Records, the album was later distributed internationally, including a release on Epic Records in the Netherlands, indicating its broader appeal beyond Australia.
